tagline: Up the St. Johns from spring to spring.
intro: From Sanford the corridor heads through DeBary to DeLand and beyond, with the St. Johns River at its heart, springs along the way and multi-use trails often running beside the road. Blue, Gemini, Green and DeLeon springs all lie on or near it.

The Timucua called the river Welaka, the River of Lakes. Spanish and English settlers, plantation owners, Civil War supply runners and steamboat tourists of the 1800s all used it after them, and pontoon boats and kayaks use it now.

moments.title: Blue Spring State Park
moments.text: The largest spring on the St. Johns holds at 73 degrees and draws manatees in winter, and Louis Thursby's 1872 house stands on a shell midden at the run's mouth.

moments.title: DeLand
moments.text: After the 1885 freeze sank baking-soda man Henry DeLand's Florida fortune, he entrusted his academy to his friend John B. Stetson, a hatmaker, and its teams are the Hatters.

moments.title: De Leon Springs
moments.text: No record ties Ponce de Leon to this spring, which took his name in the 1880s to draw tourists, and the rebuilt sugar mill beside it has been a pancake restaurant since 1961.
